title: The autumn moon
translation: The autumn moon is beautiful beyond anything. Some people say the moon is always like that and can't see the difference. That's just sad.
original: {秋|あき}の{月|つき}は{限|かぎ}りなくめでたきものなり。
いつとても{月|つき}はかくこそあれとて、{思|おも}ひ{分|わ}かざらむ{人|ひと}は、{無下|むげ}に{心|こころ}うかるべきことなり。
literal: The autumn moon is a limitlessly splendid thing.
A person who, saying 'At any time the moon is like this', does not tell (it) apart, is surely terribly pitiful.

notes.text: In Japanese poetry, the moon belongs to autumn. The full moon of mid-autumn was the moon of the year, and people sat up to watch it. For the moon in other seasons and moods, see section 137.
{思|おも}ひ{分|わ}く: 'to tell apart, to see the difference'. ざら is the negative ず, and む makes it general: 'whoever cannot tell'.

notes.quote: 無下に心うかるべきことなり
notes.text: {無下|むげ}に: 'utterly'. {心|こころ}うし: 'wretched, sad to see'. べき adds 'surely'. The verdict is on the person, not on the moon.
